A1.justification: Both PDFs describe OTTER, with matching core architecture, experiments and appendices. Their text, equations, tables and figures are readable, supporting a reliable comparison despite substantive revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original physical-robot and simulation results, component ablations and encoder-scaling experiments. These include OTTER outcomes distinct from explicitly borrowed baseline scores.

after.justification: V4 retains original robot and simulation experiments and adds physical evaluation of human-video pretraining in Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 3.1, Equation 4 changes the reported aggregation rule by adding 2D sine-cosine positional embeddings to visual value features before text-weighted aggregation. The frozen CLIP encoders, attention pooling and causal policy architecture remain.

E1.justification: V4 adds human-video pretraining using 15.6k trajectories from DexYCB and HOI4D, covering third-person grasping and egocentric manipulation. This substantially extends training coverage beyond robotic demonstrations. The original LIBERO and physical-robot evaluation tasks remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the matched experiments is unchanged. Both π0-Fast-Droid and its fine-tuned variant already appear in v1 Tables 1–2; v4 adds their descriptions rather than new comparison rows. The human-pretraining experiment uses the existing unpretrained OTTER as its control.

E3.justification: Table 3 changes from 300 in-distribution and 100 unseen trials to 50 trials for each of 30 and 10 tasks. V1 Table 7 specifies CLIP ViT-L/14, context 12 and prediction horizon 12; v4 Table 8 specifies separate simulation settings of ViT-L/32, context 4 and horizon 1. V4 also introduces human pretraining followed by robot fine-tuning. These are reported protocol changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 5 tests whether human-video pretraining benefits familiar and unseen physical tasks through a with/without-pretraining comparison. Existing component ablations, encoder scaling, attention visualizations and Appendix D analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report success-rate means with standard errors, and the new human-pretraining comparison follows that practice. No new training-seed counts, independent training repetitions, confidence intervals or significance tests are documented. Changed evaluation sample sizes belong to E3.

E6.justification: Table 3 replaces unseen-task scores for OpenVLA from 29% to 48%, DFP-OTTER from 28% to 45%, and OTTER from 59% to 61%, alongside revised protocols; these are not established same-setting gains. Several in-distribution scores also change, and Table 4 updates OTTER’s unseen result. New Table 5 reports training/unseen scores of 67%/70% with human pretraining versus 68%/62% without it. Appendix B changes reported inference speed from 17 to 50 Hz.

T1.justification: Equation 4 revises the mathematical definition of the text-aware visual representation by including positional embeddings in the aggregated values. The other CLIP-block equations and Appendix C derivation remain unchanged; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, three introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims about frozen vision-language alignment, zero-shot manipulation generalization and scaling. Human-video transfer is presented as an additional experiment rather than a redefinition of the main contributions.

C2.justification: V4 adds interpretations linking π0-Fast-Droid’s performance to its pick-and-place-heavy training data and explaining human-pretraining transfer despite camera and coordinate-frame differences. The stated limitations concerning robot morphologies, long-horizon tasks and complex scenes are retained.

D1.justification: New Appendix C.1 documents conversion of MANO hand joints into wrist/palm states, instruction labeling and dataset composition. V4 also explains the previously tabulated π0-Fast-Droid evaluation and fine-tuning, separates real/simulation configurations, and revises the reported deployment speed. Optimizer settings, training hardware and resource-access information remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds references supporting π0, FAST, PaliGemma, positional embeddings, DexYCB, HOI4D and MANO. The related-work sections and central positioning around preserving pretrained alignment remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: V4 rewrites the introductory architecture explanation, expands baseline and results discussion, and adds Sections 5.4.1 and C.1. It also renames the broader-impact heading. Most prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: V4 adds Table 5 and expands the architecture table with separate real/simulation rows. It corrects Figure 1’s encoder labels and Figure 5’s ViT-L/14 plot annotation, supplies higher-resolution versions of Figures 2 and 7, and relocates several displays within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: V4 improves completeness through a controlled human-pretraining experiment, accompanying preparation details, and explanations of π0-Fast-Droid results already present in v1. Diagram corrections also improve clarity. The gains are limited by unresolved simulation reporting: Table 3 changes trial counts and settings, while Table 4 retains its 100-trial caption but adopts the updated OTTER score. Overall, the revision provides useful additional evidence and documentation without resolving a fundamental weakness.
